items.title: UNICEF reports 172 children killed as Lebanon ceasefire takes effect

featured_image.name: The impact of conflict on Lebanon's children - UNICEF Australia

items.description: A 10-day ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon took effect at midnight local time on April 17, offering a fragile pause in hostilities after 46 days of renewed war that has killed more than 2,100 people and displaced over one million. As the guns fell quiet, UNICEF reported that at least 172 children had been killed and 661 injured since fighting resumed on March 2, with more than 415,000 children forced from their homes.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Iran denies agreeing to hand enriched uranium to US

featured_image.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Iran

items.description:
Iran's Foreign Ministry on Friday flatly denied President Trump's assertion that Tehran had agreed to hand over its stockpile of enriched uranium to the United States, exposing a sharp public rift in fragile nuclear negotiations between the two countries.

"Iran's enriched uranium is not going to be transferred anywhere," Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei told state television. He added that the "transfer of Iran's enriched uranium to the US has never been raised in negotiations".[1][2][3]

The denial came hours after Trump told CBS News in a phone interview that Iran had "agreed to everything," including a joint operation to retrieve the country's roughly 2,000 kilograms of enriched uranium and bring it to American soil. "Our people, together with the Iranians, are going to work together to go get it. And then we'll take it to the United States," Trump said, adding that no U.S. troops would be involved.[4][5]

items.title: Trump says US has 'prohibited' Israel from bombing Lebanon

featured_image.name: Iran war live: Strait of Hormuz open ‘for remaining period of ceasefire’

items.description:
President Donald Trump declared on Friday that the United States has banned Israel from conducting further airstrikes in Lebanon, issuing his strongest public directive yet to constrain Israeli military operations as a fragile 10-day ceasefire between the two countries enters its first full day.

"Israel will not be bombing Lebanon any longer. They are PROHIBITED from doing so by the USA. Enough is enough," Trump wrote on Truth Social. The statement came as part of a broader post in which Trump also pushed back against Iran's efforts to link the Lebanon truce to ongoing U.S.-Iran ceasefire negotiations. "This deal is in no way subject to Lebanon, either, but the USA will, separately, work with Lebanon, and deal with the Hezboolah situation in an appropriate manner," he wrote.[1][2][3]

items.title: Trump says US will recover enriched uranium from Iran

featured_image.name: Trump holds situation room meeting on Iran nuclear deal ...

items.description:
President Donald Trump said on Friday that the United States plans to work jointly with Iran to recover its stockpile of enriched uranium and transport it to the US, describing the effort as a gradual process that would begin soon.

"We're going to get it together. We're going to go in with Iran, at a nice leisurely pace, and go down and start excavating with big machinery… We'll bring it back to the United States," Trump told Reuters in a phone interview. He said what he called "nuclear dust" would be retrieved "very soon," referring to enriched uranium believed to remain underground after US and Israeli strikes on Iran's nuclear facilities at Fordow and Natanz in June 2025.[1][2][3]

items.title: Iran war reshapes global energy policy as nations fast-track renewables

featured_image.name: Iran war: A global energy shock could accelerate a shift to renewables

items.description:
The escalating conflict between the United States, Israel, and Iran — now in its seventh week — is reshaping global energy policy, as countries exposed to the largest oil supply disruption in decades accelerate their pivot toward renewable power.

Iran's blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, through which roughly 20% of the world's oil and gas supply transits, has locked an estimated 13 million barrels of oil per day out of global markets. A U.S. military blockade of Iranian ports, ordered by President Donald Trump on Monday after ceasefire talks collapsed, has further choked the waterway. The twin disruptions have pushed crude prices near historic highs and laid bare the vulnerabilities of fossil fuel dependency.[1][2][3]
